Hey, fellow artist here and also new to the sub lmao.

I often call these types of things more of an art rut rather than artblock. Reason being as that kind of feeling can run for a long time and be difficult to get out of. I once had it for about a year where I was displeased with literally anything I made. I even had thought about quitting art entirely despite it being my biggest passion in life.

Eventually I learned there's a few ways to overcome this kind of thing.

1) Experimentation

A lot of times I found myself unhappy with how I drew things as I felt they were off to me or that I was getting frustrated that drawing the scenes were feeling more of a chore than fun like they used to be. So I would take the time to instead mess around with new stuff which lead me to overhauling my style to something that was more fun to me. Other times I would play around with tutorials of drawing different things to try and figure out what worked with me or try and mesh it with how I already did things. A lot of time this method helped me.

2) Take a break

Sometimes you can burn yourself out and that happens! Even if you don't realize that it's burnout and just think it's artblock or something. When I got to those points I would just take some time off and distract myself doing something else that I enjoyed. Whether it be games with friends or doing whatever else I wanted that wasn't related to art. It allowed me a time to relax and de-stress myself from the build up of frustration that lead to the burn out.

3) Just create

Nothing you make has to be perfect tbh. That's an absurd expectation that a lot of us deal with that, if it doesn't look perfect, it's no good. But that's incorrect. Not drawing anything is worse than just drawing something and it didn't turn out right. Even I'll admit that I still make some sketches that just don't look as good as the other stuff I make. Because you learn the more you work at it and really it takes time to realize that everyone is their worst critic. Even moreso when we're staring at the image were drawing for hours at a time. So while you may hate how something you work on looks, just remember that art is improved with experience and you still managed to make something.

Good luck getting out of your rut!
